newsitem.title: ITALY: FOCUS - New Sardinian gold mine sees profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - New Sardinian gold mine sees profit.

text.p: A plan for a gold mine in Sardinia once dismissed as folly turned into reality this week and the pioneer of the project said on Friday he expected it to make a profit by its second year.

Sardinia Gold Mining SpA (SGM), a 70 percent owned unit of Australian-based Gold Mines of Sardinia Ltd, poured its first gold ingot on Thursday night from the Furtei mine in the south of the Mediterranean island.
"It's no longer a dream, it's reality," said Giampiero Pinna, chairman of the Ente Minerario Sardo (Sardinian Mining Body), which discovered the deposit and holds 30 percent of SGM.
Pinna told Reuters by telephone that the mine had produced 50 kg (110 lbs) of gold in the two months since output began and had now poured its first six kg (13 lb) ingot.
"We foresee output of one tonne per year and turnover of 20 billion lire ($12 million)," he said.
By the third or fourth year, Pinna said the Furtei mine should be capable of producing two tonnes of gold and doubling its turnover.
"Break-even will be when we hit turnover of around 15 billion lire," he said. "From the second year the company should be in profit."
SGM is also planning to mine what is expected to be a world-class reserve at Osilo in the north of the island.
"It will be double Furtei," Pinna said. "We expect it to start production in 1999."
Furtei is the only working gold mine in Italy and the biggest in western Europe to extract so-called "invisible" gold which is only visible through a microscope.
Pinna said there was a small mine in Spain which produced the same kind of gold and other similar ones in Canada, the United States and Australia.
But gold mining in western Europe has been dying out. One mine in northern Italy closed more than 35 years ago because it was uneconomic and another in France has also ceased production.
Gold Mines of Sardinia said in a statement production of the ingot was "an historic event representing the first gold produced in Sardinia and Italy in modern times".
"Geological programmes being carried out on the Furtei Project are encouraging and the directors are confident that additional reserves will be outlined in the Furtei area," it said in a statement.
Pinna has championed the project from the outset as managing director of Progemisa, the exploration arm of Ente Minerario Sardo of which he was formerly managing director.
Progemisa began work in the early 1990s and exploration cost 12 billion lire, Pinna said. A further 25 billion lire has since been invested to exploit the reserves.
"We had to overcome a great deal of scepticism, it was tough," he said. "Everyone was sceptical, until yesterday.
"If it (production) hadn't happened, I think they would have thrown me into the sea." ($1=1697 lire)
